title: bug: JetBrains STATE_SNAPSHOT project check deletes daemon.json and reconnects when a WSL-hosted daemon spells this project /mnt/<d>/...
description:
Found by architect-4ae016fb on 2026-10-30, while planning task-6fc0096b. It is the same bug class, one stage later: after the /health probe instead of before it.

What the code does
- MoeMessageDispatcher.handle, STATE_SNAPSHOT branch (moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeMessageDispatcher.kt, about lines 83-96), compares File(newState.project.rootPath).canonicalPath with File(project.basePath).canonicalPath.
- On a mismatch it deletes .moe/daemon.json unconditionally, then calls onProjectMismatch: disconnect, then scheduleReconnect.

Repro on Windows
- The project is D:/proj. A WSL agent's pre-flight started its daemon with --project /mnt/d/proj, so the snapshot's rootPath is /mnt/d/proj.
- On Windows, File('/mnt/d/proj').canonicalPath is D:\mnt\d\proj, so the check fails.
- The plugin deletes the live daemon.json and reconnects. The reconnect spawns a second daemon over the same .moe/.

After task-6fc0096b, readDaemonInfo, the reachability checks and the /health probe all accept that daemon as this project. This check is the one deleter left on that path.

Wanted
- Judge rootPath with task-6fc0096b's same-project rule, MoeDaemonSupervisor.isSameProject: comparableProjectPath first, then canonicalPath. Do not add another normalizer.
- A genuinely different rootPath still disconnects and reconnects, as today.
- Remove daemon.json only through MoeDaemonSupervisor.deleteDaemonInfoIfUnchanged, against the DaemonInfo the client connected with, never unconditionally. The dispatcher holds no supervisor, so do the removal in MoeProjectService's onProjectMismatch.
- When planning, serialize with CQ-RF04 (task-de91373a): it also edits MoeProjectService.kt (restartDaemon).

Out of scope
- VS Code (task-80ed1fe8).
- restartDaemon.
definitionOfDone: A STATE_SNAPSHOT whose rootPath names this project in a drive, forward-slash, /mnt/<d> or //wsl$ spelling neither deletes daemon.json nor disconnects. A JetBrains test shows it.
A STATE_SNAPSHOT for another project still disconnects and reconnects. daemon.json is removed only while it still parses to the DaemonInfo the client connected with. Tests show both.
JetBrains tests pass under the jetbrains-gradle lease: from WSL, cmd.exe gradlew.bat test --rerun.
